title: Hack Club
description: A nonprofit network of 20,000+ teenage hackers and coding clubs worldwide, running a continuous slate of free, mostly-online hackathons and coding challenges (recent examples include Aria, an algorithmic music-coding competition, and OrpheusAthon, a one-hour coding event) alongside 1,500+ in-person school clubs and a large teen Slack community. The organization's own site states it is 'free for every teenager, forever,' for 'all teens aged 13-18... anywhere on Earth.' Some specific named events are in-person and location-restricted (e.g. Snowglobe, an all-girls hackathon held in San Francisco) -- this record covers Hack Club's broader online hackathon/challenge activity, not any single in-person event.
current_cycle_label: Ongoing -- Hack Club runs a rotating slate of online hackathons/challenges throughout the year rather than a single fixed event; check hackclub.com for what's currently running

title: Global Appathon
organization: App Inventor Foundation / MIT App Inventor
description: A free, virtual hackathon hosted by the App Inventor Foundation and MIT App Inventor, where participants build mobile apps addressing the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals using MIT App Inventor. Six age categories cover Junior (under 13), Youth (13-17), Adult (18+), and All-Ages teams, with placement based on age as of a stated date each cycle. The most recent cycle drew 2,176 participants from 141 countries and regions. Explicitly open to anyone in the world except U.S.-embargoed countries and regions (Iran, Cuba, Syria, North Korea, and Crimea/Donetsk/Luhansk areas of Ukraine).
residency_restrictions: Open worldwide except U.S.-embargoed countries/regions (Iran, Cuba, Syria, North Korea, Crimea/Donetsk/Luhansk areas of Ukraine) -- Turkey is not among the excluded countries
application_requirements: Participants may only make one submission and cannot be on multiple teams

title: Discover Model United Nations (DMUN)
description: A non-profit initiative running a series of free, high-quality online Model United Nations conferences, letting students worldwide practice diplomatic negotiation, public speaking, and international-relations research entirely from home. The organization's own page describes its events as 'youth-led events that are free, online, and accessible to all youths.'
